title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: Given an array of k linked lists, each sorted in ascending order, merge them into one sorted linked list.

reference.use_case: Combining many already-sorted streams into one sorted stream, such as merging sorted data files on disk or time-ordered results from many shards.
system_examples: LSM-tree storage engines (RocksDB, LevelDB, Cassandra) — compaction merges multiple sorted SSTables into one
Database external sorting (e.g. PostgreSQL tuplesort) — merges sorted runs spilled to disk
Distributed search (Elasticsearch coordinating node) — merges per-shard sorted hits into a global result
reference.explanation: A min-heap holding the current head of each list yields the next smallest element in O(log k), so merging N elements costs O(N log k) instead of O(N·k); pairwise divide-and-conquer merging achieves the same bound. k-way merge is the backbone of LSM compaction, external sorting, and scatter-gather queries.
